hook: Ordered hydronium-water layers on gold create new electronic states that photoemission can see.
summary: Angle-resolved photoemission on Au(111) revealed parabolic interfacial states when water formed ordered Eigen- or Zundel-type hydronium layers, unlike disordered water, which is insulating. Calculations trace them to gold's surface state with a lighter effective mass. The layers form only at 120-140 K in vacuum, far from real electrochemical conditions.
title: Evolution of Interfacial States Induced by Hydronium–Water Ordering on Au(111)
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
